result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers pick a left sidebar with one group per page and a drill-down list on phones. A gives more you could build from: it handles the big, table-heavy groups (team, vehicles, alert rules) with full-width tables and frozen name columns, turns those tables into stacked cards on phones, and keeps anchor links inside long groups. B adds useful ideas, such as merging alerts with notifications, stable URLs for each group, and sub-tabs inside Billing. But it says little about large groups beyond the integrations grid. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers pick a sidebar with one group per page and a drill-down list on phones. B goes further on the larger groups: tables can fill the width with frozen name columns, tables turn into stacked cards on phones, and integrations becomes a single column. B also explains the sidebar order by how often people visit and finds a real use for the dev's anchor-link idea. A is clear and buildable, but it gives less detail on how the large groups (team members, vehicles) are handled and on why the content is structured the way it is.
